title: Lemon ricotta cake
subtitle: a dense, moist Italian-style cake with a fine crumb and sharp lemon flavour
excerpt: Ricotta makes this cake unusually moist and tender with a very fine, close crumb. The texture is somewhere between a cheesecake and a sponge: denser than a Victoria sponge but lighter than a cheesecake. The lemon flavour comes from both the zest and juice in the batter. It keeps well for three days and is excellent with a spoonful of crème fraîche.
sourceNotes: Lemon ricotta cake, an Italian-style cake widely adapted in British home baking from the early 2000s. Method from standard contemporary British patisserie practice.

glossaryTerms.definition: Fresh ricotta adds moisture, protein, and a mild dairy flavour to cakes without making them heavy. It is used in Italian-style cakes to give a fine, moist crumb.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Keeps in an airtight tin for up to 3 days. The lemon flavour deepens on the second day.

content.text: in the batter keeps the crumb moist without adding cream or oil. The cake has a flat, even top (it does not dome) and a fine-grained texture. Use full-fat ricotta for the best texture; low-fat ricotta has more water and can make the cake slightly gummy.
Heat the oven to 160°C fan. Grease and line a 20 cm round cake tin with baking parchment.
Beat the butter and caster sugar together until pale and fluffy, about 3 to 4 minutes with a hand mixer or stand mixer.
Add the eggs one at a time, beating well after each addition. If the mixture looks like it is curdling, add a tablespoon of the flour.
Beat in the ricotta, lemon zest, and lemon juice until just combined. The batter may look slightly curdled; this is normal.
Fold in the flour and baking powder until just combined. Do not over-mix.

Spoon into the prepared tin and bake for 40 to 45 minutes until a skewer inserted in the centre comes out clean and the cake is golden on top and springs back when lightly pressed. Cool in the tin for 20 minutes before turning out. Dust with icing sugar to serve.

attrs.problem: Cake gummy in the centre after baking time
attrs.avoid: Avoid using very wet ricotta; if the ricotta is sitting in liquid, drain it through a sieve for 30 minutes first.
attrs.fix: Return the cake to the oven for a further 10 minutes and check again; the centre should feel just set to the touch.

attrs.problem: Cake browning quickly but raw in the middle
attrs.avoid: Avoid oven temperatures above 160°C fan for this cake; the ricotta content makes it bake more slowly than a standard sponge.
attrs.fix: Cover the top loosely with foil and continue baking until the skewer comes out clean.
